_meta.description: Blind out-of-sample backtest of the master trees against the 2000-2010 corpus.
_meta.protocol: Wines withheld from predicting agents; ground truth resolved independently by separate agents that never saw predictions; deterministic synonym-aware matching.
_meta.trees_as_of: outputs/master_trees/ at commit time; trees synthesised from 2011-2025 (this corpus is unseen)

2000_p1_q1.tree_branch: Branch 2: 'Same country' questions > Sub-branch: same country, different single varieties, origin-heavy. The tree's leaf gives STRONG SIGNAL France/Italy as candidate countries; here the stem already fixes the country as France, so the sub-branch's France variety distribution is applied directly.

2000_p1_q2.tree_branch: Branch 1: Same single grape variety > Sub-branch: 3-4 wines, origin and maturity/quality heavily marked > Leaf (default). NO MATCHING BRANCH for the stem's 'rank the wines by price' instruction — the tree has no leaf keyed to a price-ranking task; applying the default variety leaf for the shared-variety ID and treating 'climatic and winemaking influences' as a soft match to the tree's style-driven leaves.

2000_p1_q3.tree_branch: Branch 1: Same single grape variety > Sub-branch: 3-4 wines, origin and maturity/quality heavily marked > Leaf (default), with Riesling promoted to top rank due to the stem's explicit residual-sugar question (RS variance across wines is a classic Riesling exam marker not covered by a dedicated tree leaf — flagged as an inference beyond the tree's literal wording).

2001_p1_q1.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH — the tree has no leaf for 'all single varietal wines' without an assertion of shared variety across the flight. Closest analogue is Branch 4 (mixed-bag / different countries, different varieties, no linking constraint), but that branch's evidence base is specifically the paper's *final* question slot, whereas this is Q1 — an atypical position mismatch, flagged.

2001_p1_q2.tree_branch: Branch 1: Same single grape variety > Sub-branch: 2-wine same-variety questions with winemaking emphasis > Leaf (default), since the stem states 'same country' but does not specify Old World vs New World framing needed for the more specific sub-leaf.

2001_p1_q3.tree_branch: Branch 4: mixed-bag / different countries, different varieties > Sub-branch: identification marks high, no linking constraint. Positional mismatch flagged: this is Q3 of 4 questions, not the paper's final slot where this branch's evidence base sits.

2001_p1_q4.tree_branch: Branch 3: same region / pair-comparison questions > Sub-branch: same region + quality/vintage differentiation. NO leaf exists for the stem's added constraint of 'same producer' (an even tighter link than the tree's evidence base assumes) — flagged.

2002_p1_q1.tree_branch: Branch 1: Same single grape variety > Sub-branch: 3-4 wines... Leaf (stem says 'different countries' or 'two countries'). NO MATCHING BRANCH exactly for the stem's 'two variety-pairs across the same two countries' double structure — the tree has no leaf for a paired 2x2 variety/country grid; applying the different-countries leaf twice (once per variety pair) as the closest fit, flagged.

2002_p1_q2.tree_branch: Branch 1: Same single grape variety > Sub-branch: 3-4 wines... Leaf (stem says 'different countries' or 'two countries') — exact match, stem explicitly states 'each is from a different country of origin' for a 3-wine same-variety flight.

2002_p1_q3.tree_branch: Branch 4: mixed-bag / different countries, different varieties > Sub-branch: identification marks high, no linking constraint — exact structural match ('five different single grape varieties and five different countries') AND positionally correct as the paper's final question (wines 8-12 of 12), matching the tree's 'examiner pattern' note that the closing P1 slot is the recurring curveball.

2003_p1_q4.tree_branch: Branch 4: mixed-bag / different countries, different varieties > Sub-branch: identification marks high, no linking constraint — matches structurally ('each made from a different single grape variety') and positionally, as this is the paper's final question (wines 10-12).

2000_p3_q1.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH — tree has no leaf for 'internationally recognised labels' + MLF/oak-focused stems lacking sparkling, sweet, fortified, or rosé signals. Not Branch 1 (no sparkling cue), not Branch 2 (no RS cue), not Branch 3 (no fortified cue), not Branch 5 (no explicit mixed-bag/classification cue). Closest by elimination is a generic still-white oaked-Chardonnay reading, not a tree leaf.

2000_p3_q2.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH — tree has no leaf for a bare 'same single grape variety, multiple countries, comment on style and quality' stem with no RS/sweetness/sparkling/fortified cue attached. Closest analog is the single-grape-cross-country evidence pattern underlying Branch 2, but without the explicit RS/alcohol trigger that Branch 2 requires to fire.

2000_p3_q3.tree_branch: Branch 2: residual sugar / sweet wine mechanism questions — sub-branch 'explicit RS and alcohol asked' leaf (RS in g/L plus 'key elements of the production process to show how sweetness has been achieved' is exactly the mechanism-diagnosis ask this leaf is built for).

2001_p3_q1.tree_branch: Branch 2: residual sugar / sweet wine mechanism questions — sub-branch 'explicit RS and alcohol asked' leaf. Stem asks botrytis presence, RS, alcohol, acidity balance, and ageing potential across 6 wines — a near-exact match to this leaf's evidence pattern.

2001_p3_q2.tree_branch: Intersection of Branch 4 ('compare styles from one region,' sub-branch leaf) and Branch 2's region distribution (German Prädikat ladder). Stem fixes country, region, AND grape variety as constant, then asks RS per wine — this is the single-region, single-grape, RS-ladder structure the tree associates with German Prädikat estates.

2001_p3_q3.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH — tree has no leaf for a bare 'origin + alcohol level + quality' stem without sweetness, bubbles, or fortification cues. Leaning toward Branch 3 (fortified/oxidative) only because alcohol is singled out as its own sub-question, which elsewhere in the tree correlates with fortified/high-strength styles, but this is inference, not a matched leaf.

2002_p3_q1.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH — tree has no leaf for Bordeaux grape varieties appearing in Paper 3. This is structurally the same phenomenon flagged in the tree's Curveball Cases ('2018 P3 Q3: Rhone-associated varieties in Paper 3 rather than Paper 2') but for Bordeaux varieties instead of Rhone ones — no dedicated leaf exists.

2002_p3_q2.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH — same gap as 2000_p3_q2: 'single grape variety, three countries, ageing and quality' with no sweetness/sparkling/fortified cue does not trigger any Layer A branch.

2002_p3_q3.tree_branch: Branch 4: same region producing multiple styles — sub-branch 'compare styles from one region' leaf. Stem fixes 'same country of origin' then asks per-wine style ID plus 'key points in winemaking which most contribute to the wine's style... highlighting the differences from the other wines in the flight' — an almost verbatim match to this leaf's language.

2002_p3_q4.tree_branch: Branch 4: same region producing multiple styles — sub-branch 'compare styles from one region' leaf, same match as 2002_p3_q3 (identical stem template, different wine set — 'Wines 10-12... same country of origin... style... key points in winemaking which most contribute... highlighting the differences').

2003_p3_q1.tree_branch: Branch 2: residual sugar / sweet wine mechanism questions — sub-branch 'explicit RS and alcohol asked' leaf, combined with the single-grape-cross-country structure. 'Same single grape variety... different country of origin... alcohol... residual sugar... elements of production which most influence style' matches this leaf closely.

2003_p3_q2.tree_branch: Branch 4: same region producing multiple styles — sub-branch 'Same producer, different style' leaf ('keep vintage, lees age, fortification timing, oxidation regime, and dosage/RS as the decision levers rather than changing country'). Stem fixes 'same country and region,' then asks vintage ID and maturity per wine, matching this leaf's vintage-as-decision-lever framing.

2003_p3_q3.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH (weak partial match to Branch 5's anti-collapse rule) — stem gives 'four different countries, maturity, elements of production which most influence style' with no explicit sparkling/sweet/fortified/rosé/classification cue, so no leaf fires cleanly. Where it loosely echoes anything, it is Branch 5's instruction not to collapse a mixed-bag prediction onto one grape family, but the stem lacks Branch 5's defining classification/commercial-emphasis trigger.

2004_p3_q1.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH — tree has no leaf for a two-vintages-of-the-same-wine vertical comparison. Conceptually adjacent to Branch 6's paired-contrast structure, but Branch 6 pairs are built on a production-METHOD fork (dosage, cask vs bottle ageing, classified vs unclassified) within a shared origin, not a vintage fork, and Branch 6 is founded on a single 2026 instance far outside this paper's era.

2004_p3_q2.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH — identical gap to 2004_p3_q1 (another 'two different vintages of the same wine' pair, no tree leaf for vertical-vintage comparisons).

2004_p3_q3.tree_branch: Branch 1: P3 Q1 / sparkling-led opening flights — sub-branch 'explicit sparkling, often non-Champagne' default leaf. Stem states 'Wines 5-8 are all sparkling wines' outright, with quality discussed 'with reference to the time spent on lees' — the exact traditional-method-vs-tank-method contrast the leaf is built for.

2004_p3_q4.tree_branch: Branch 5: rose/unusual still/mixed-bag P3 questions — sub-branch 'mixed bag with classification/commercial emphasis' leaf. Stem states 'Wines 9-12 are a mixed bag' verbatim, matching the leaf's exact evidence category.

2005_p3_q1.tree_branch: Branch 5: rose/unusual still/mixed-bag P3 questions — sub-branch 'mixed bag with classification/commercial emphasis' leaf (weaker match than 2004_p3_q4). The 'discuss and compare the quality of each wine within a commercial context' phrase echoes this leaf's commercial-framing trigger; the explicit alcohol-level sub-question also loosely echoes Branch 3's fortified association, so this is a two-way call.

2005_p3_q2.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH — tree has no leaf for 'same single grape, same country/region, consecutive-but-not-necessarily-chronological vintages' (a pure vertical vintage-variation flight). Closest partial analogs are Branch 4 (same region producing multiple STYLES) and Branch 2 (sweet-wine mechanism), but neither matches a single-style vertical construction.

2005_p3_q3.tree_branch: NO MATCHING BRANCH — Branch 6 ('multi-pair same-region flight') requires each pair to share country AND region; here pairing is by SAME PRODUCER with two DIFFERENT countries represented overall, an inverse structure the tree has no leaf for.
